name: Visceral Calciphylaxis
aliases: Calcific Uremic Arteriolopathy with Visceral Involvement

criteria.description: Histopathological evidence of medial calcification and intimal proliferation in small to medium-sized visceral arteries
Clinical or radiologic evidence of ischemic injury or infarction in visceral organs (e.g., bowel, pancreas)
Presence of risk factors such as end-stage renal disease, hyperparathyroidism, or elevated serum calcium-phosphate product
Exclusion of other causes of visceral ischemia such as embolism or vasculitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of vascular calcification in visceral arteries plus clinical or imaging evidence of visceral organ ischemia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires biopsy; imaging and clinical findings support diagnosis in high-risk patients.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cutaneous calciphylaxis lesions with visceral involvement
pathognomonic.notes: Skin lesions often precede visceral symptoms

imaging: CT or MRI showing visceral organ ischemia or infarction
Vascular calcifications on plain radiographs or CT
Angiography demonstrating arterial narrowing or occlusion
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified
other: Histopathology showing medial calcification and intimal proliferation in small to medium-sized arteries

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of vascular calcification on histology
Presence of inflammatory infiltrates in vessel walls

redFlags: Severe refractory abdominal pain in patient with renal failure
Presence of cutaneous calciphylaxis lesions with systemic symptoms
